react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on a single biological story: the tryptophan metabolic network is profoundly perturbed in the treatment group. RaMP-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as the top hit with FDR 9.58e-15 and fold-enrichment 667, covering six input metabolites (L-tryptophan, tryptamine, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and indoleacetaldehyde). MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirmed the same KEGG pathway (hsa00380) at p = 1.59e-08 with an identical six-compound overlap out of 41 pathway members. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm ranked 'Tryptophan metabolism' first at p = 0.000168, mapping seven of the input compounds including all six above plus the user-supplied C00127 (annotated by mummichog as glutathione disulfide — a namespace artefact, not a structural conflict). Downstream of the core pathway, RaMP also returned Reactome R-HSA-209931 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis' (FDR 6.64e-08, fold-enrichment 1200.9) and WikiPathways WP:WP550 'Biogenic amine synthesis' (FDR 6.64e-08), both consistent with a tryptophan origin. The affected driver metabolites span the full tryptophan catabolic spectrum: the parent amino acid (L-tryptophan), its decarboxylated product (tryptamine), the kynurenine-pathway intermediate (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid), the indoleacetaldehyde shunt, and the two downstream neuroendocrine effectors (serotonin and melatonin). The doxycycline-acrolein axis is biologically plausible as an oxidative stress trigger that diverts tryptophan flux away from the serotonergic-melatonergic branch toward kynurenine-pathway products such as 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway. RaMP-DB multi-database ORA ranks KEGG:map00380 first with FDR 9.58e-15 and six input metabolites (indol-3-ylacetaldehyde, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, tryptamine, L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin), followed by WP:WP465 (FDR 1.14e-14) and REACT:R-HSA-209931 'Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis' (FDR 6.64e-08). MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirms KEGG:hsa00380 (p-value 1.59e-08) with the identical six-compound overlap out of 41 pathway members. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently recovers MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism (p-value 0.000168) with seven mapped compounds including all six above plus C00127 annotated as glutathione disulfide — a namespace artefact since the user-supplied C00127 is cytidine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate (InChIKey NMPZCCZXCOMSDQ). The driver compounds span two tryptophan branches: the serotonergic-melatonergic arm (L-tryptophan, tryptamine, serotonin, melatonin hit REACT:R-HSA-209931 and WP:WP550) and the kynurenine arm (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and indoleacetaldehyde). The remaining four input compounds — doxycycline, acrolein, milrinone, and the misannotated C00127 — do not appear in any enriched pathway.
